precepts.text: The spies returned after forty days, and Caleb stilled the people before Moses: let us go up at once and possess it, for we are well able to overcome it.
precepts.point: So Moses sware on that day that the land whereon Caleb's feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever, because he wholly followed the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
Caleb tells Joshua, “Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me from Kadesh–barnea to espy out the land; and I brought him word again as it was in mine heart.” Here is that word. “And they returned from searching of the land after forty days”, came to Moses, Aaron and all the congregation at Kadesh, “and shewed them the fruit of the land.” The land “floweth with milk and honey”, but “the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.” The Amalekites in the south, the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites in the mountains, the Canaanites by the sea and by the coast of Jordan.

Then Caleb: “And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.” That is the word as it was in his heart. Caleb was not playing any games; he was about that business, ready to go and take the land, because he understood the Most High had already promised us the land, so he had no fear. That is the spirit that says, let us go up at once and possess it, and that is what wholly following the Lord looks like.

precepts.text: The men that went up with him brought an evil report of giants, saying we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and made the people afraid.
precepts.point: So Moses sware on that day that the land whereon Caleb's feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever, because he wholly followed the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless my brethren that went up with me made the heart of the people melt”. This is how they did it. “But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.” They “brought up an evil report of the land”, calling it “a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof”, full of “men of a great stature”; “there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”

The men that went with Caleb brought up an evil report, made the people afraid, and made them doubt. Caleb alone “wholly followed the Lord my God”, and that is why Moses sware that day that the land his feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever.

precepts.text: Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
precepts.point: The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
Caleb at fourscore and five is “as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me”, an eighty-five-year-old man in perfect health. Moses was the same way: “And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.” A hundred and twenty years old with the strength and the vision of a young man.

A lot of us are not living to a hundred and twenty, but at the same time we are making it to sixty and seventy, and at fifty we are hooked up on machines. We are all going to die at some point, but that does not mean you have to be miserable, sitting there hooked up to all kind of machines while you are here.

precepts.text: There is no riches above a sound body; do not spend your years on the earth in continual sickness.
precepts.point: The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
“Health and good estate of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth. There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart. Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.” Caleb had that sound body at eighty-five, with his strength “for war, both to go out, and to come in.”

Do not spend your years on the earth in continual sickness. Leadership has been pushing that we all need to take care of our bodies and our health. A lot of us deal with gluttony even though it is not a topic we talk about all the time; cut down a little what you eat and eat better food.

precepts.text: Be quick in all thy works, including how you eat, so shall there no sickness come unto thee.
precepts.point: The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
“My son, hear me, and despise me not, and at the last thou shalt find as I told thee: in all thy works be quick, so shall there no sickness come unto thee.” Be quick in all thy works, and that includes how you eat.

The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live. Caleb's strength at eighty-five was the same as in the day Moses sent him; that is the health the Most High keeps for those who are quick.

precepts.text: The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim.
precepts.point: The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, so that ten tribes went to Jeroboam. If Jeroboam would walk in the ways of the Most High and keep his statutes, the Most High would build him a sure house as he built for David. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim”. So when Solomon, “seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph”, Jeroboam was set over two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh.

Jeroboam the son of Nebat was “a mighty man of valour”, and he lifted up his hand against the king. The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him in the way, rent his new garment in twelve pieces, and said, “Take thee ten pieces”. The Most High would rend ten tribes out of Solomon's hand and give them to Jeroboam, leaving one tribe “for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake”. The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, and the ten tribes went to Jeroboam.

points: The countries in the land of Canaan were distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes, by lot, as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half tribe; Moses had already given the two tribes and a half their inheritance on the other side Jordan.

points: The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, therefore no part was given unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dwell in with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance.
The Levites were living in the suburbs, which is the towns, right among the people. They did not have a land designated to themselves; they were spread throughout all the many tribes.
